response.sql:
WITH rental_store AS (
  SELECT r.rental_id, i.store_id, SUM(p.amount) AS rental_total, COUNT(*) AS payment_count
  FROM payment p
  JOIN rental r ON r.rental_id = p.rental_id
  JOIN inventory i ON i.inventory_id = r.inventory_id
  WHERE p.amount > 4.99
  GROUP BY r.rental_id, i.store_id
)
SELECT store_id, AVG(rental_total) AS avg_rental_total, AVG(payment_count) AS avg_payments_per_rental
FROM rental_store
GROUP BY store_id
ORDER BY store_id;

assumptions.assumption: The 4.99 threshold applies to each individual payment amount (amount > 4.99), not to the summed total per rental.

Payments are linked to rentals only through payment.rental_id, and rentals to stores only through rental.inventory_id -> inventory.store_id. Inner joins drop payments with NULL rental_id or no matching rental.
Each rental has exactly one inventory item and therefore exactly one store, so grouping by rental and store gives the same rentals as grouping by rental alone.
The per-store averages are taken over rentals that have at least one qualifying payment; rentals with no payment above 4.99 are not counted.
